details:
**Trapped under a mountain for 500 years**
After losing his bet with the Buddha, the Monkey King Sun Wukong is pinned under the Five Elements Mountain for five centuries. He is freed only when the monk Xuanzang (Tang Sanzang) passes by, and in return he must protect the monk on the pilgrimage to India.

**Ruyi Jingu Bang (the size-changing staff)**
This is Sun Wukong's magic iron staff, which can grow or shrink at will. It began as an iron pillar used to measure the depth of the sea, kept in the undersea palace of the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea, Ao Guang. The pillar glowed when its rightful owner arrived, and it weighs 13,500 jin. Sun Wukong can shrink it to the size of a needle and keep it behind his ear.

**Zhu Bajie ("Pigsy") and his nine-toothed iron rake**
Zhu Bajie is a gluttonous, lustful pig-man who carries a nine-toothed rake and is often called "the idiot." He was once Marshal Tianpeng, commander of Heaven's river navy, but was banished for flirting with the Moon Goddess and reborn with a pig's form. He lived in the Cloud Pathway Cave and tried to marry a village elder's daughter at Gao Village until his huge appetite gave him away. At the end of the novel he becomes the "Cleanser of the Altars," so he can eat leftover offerings.

**Sha Wujing ("Sandy") and the smashed crystal goblet**
Sha Wujing was once the Curtain-Lifting General in Heaven. He was beaten 800 times with a rod and exiled after he accidentally broke the Queen Mother's crystal goblet (a vase in some versions) at the Peach Banquet. As a monstrous sand demon wearing a necklace of skulls, he terrorized travelers at a river crossing until he joined the pilgrims.

**Urinating on the Buddha's fingers (the palm wager)**
Sun Wukong bets the Buddha that he can leap out of his palm. He somersaults to what he thinks is the edge of the universe, sees five huge pillars, and writes his name on one and urinates on it. The pillars turn out to be the Buddha's fingers. Sun Wukong has also mastered 72 transformations, while Pigsy knows 36.

**Tang Sanzang / Xuanzang, the "Golden Cicada"**
The monk at the center of the pilgrimage, also called Tripitaka or Tang Seng, is based on the real 7th-century monk Xuanzang. He is the reincarnation of the Buddha's disciple Golden Cicada, so demons keep attacking him because eating his flesh is said to grant immortality. An early episode tells how his mother pretends to donate 100 pairs of shoes so she can meet her son. He had proven who he was with a letter written in blood.

**Peaches of immortality, "Protector of the Horses," and "Great Sage Equal to Heaven"**
To calm Sun Wukong down, Heaven gives him the lowly job of Protector (Keeper) of the Horses. Insulted, he rebels and calls himself the "Great Sage Equal to Heaven," which angers the Jade Emperor. He then eats the peaches of immortality and disrupts the Queen Mother's Peach Banquet, and that rampage leads to his punishment by the Buddha.

**Book of Life and Death**
When Sun Wukong's soul is dragged to the underworld, he crosses his own name, and the names of his monkey followers, out of the register that records lifespans. This makes him immortal.

**Vulture Peak scriptures and the 81 tribulations**
The pilgrims must survive 81 trials, including a lair of spider spirits. At the end they receive the Buddhist scriptures from the Buddha at Vulture Peak. In the final trial the scriptures fall into a river and get soaked.

**Golden headband and the tightening spell**
The bodhisattva Guanyin arranges the pilgrimage and its disciples. She has Sun Wukong tricked into wearing a golden headband. Whenever Xuanzang chants a spell, the band tightens and gives the Monkey King a crushing headache, which is how the monk controls him.

**Born from a stone egg / Water Curtain Cave**
Sun Wukong hatches from a stone egg on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He becomes king of the monkeys after jumping through a waterfall and finding the Water Curtain Cave behind it, which becomes the monkeys' home.

**"Fiery eyes and golden gaze"**
Laozi tries to destroy Sun Wukong by sealing him in his Eight Trigrams Furnace for 49 days. He survives, and the smoke leaves him with fiery eyes that can see through disguises. He uses them, for example, to recognize the shape-shifting White Bone Spirit, who disguises herself as a young girl and old people.

**Kingdom of Women and the pregnancy river**
On the way west, Xuanzang and Pigsy drink from a river whose water makes anyone who drinks it pregnant. This happens near the Kingdom of Women, a land with no men whose queen wants to marry the monk.

**Arthur Waley's *Monkey***
Arthur Waley's famous abridged English translation of the novel is simply titled *Monkey*, and it popularized the names "Sandy" and "Pigsy." Gerald Vizenor's novel *Griever* is a modern adaptation of the story.

**Wu Cheng'en and the Four Great Classical Novels**
This 100-chapter novel from the Ming dynasty is usually credited to Wu Cheng'en. It is one of China's Four Great Classical Novels, along with *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, *Water Margin*, and *Dream of the Red Chamber*.
